defect.summary: Eng's per-class diagnostic label was built as `key.replace("\u0000", "/")` — DERIVED FROM THE GROUPING KEY. T13 changed that key to the shared length-prefixed encoding and left the display line, so two things broke in one commit: ① ordinary labels became raw keys ("15:MICA/SubjectLog14:TOOL_ATTEMPTED" where an operator used to read "MICA/SubjectLog/TOOL_ATTEMPTED"), and ② a NUL INSIDE a component is rewritten to "/", so a class prints under the name of a DIFFERENT class whose component genuinely contains a slash — measured at the relayed bytes: three distinct buckets, TWO distinct labels. FIX: derive the label from the FIRST RECORD IN THE BUCKET, not from the key — `JSON.stringify([bucket[0].moduleId, bucket[0].eventType])`. The key is for grouping and the label is for a human; they are separate concerns and T13 proved they were coupled. JSON escaping is unambiguous by construction and stays readable, which the key never promised to be — it was readable only by accident of the delimiter it used.
defect.ground: Codex cold read of T13 at dcee656, ARC_MICA-VERIFY_T13-Class-Key-1_20261001, verdict PASS-WITH-FINDINGS, finding F1: "two different classes can now be printed with the same `eventClass` label … a real output defect". REPRODUCED at the relayed bytes by the build seat 2026-10-01 21:5xZ: three buckets, labels ["1:a3:b/c", "1:a3:b/c", "1:m1:e"], and ordinary records reading "15:MICA/SubjectLog14:TOOL_ATTEMPTED". ⛔ AND THE DEFECT IS LIVE: /opt/mica-machine is VINTAGE dcee656 as of 2026-10-01 21:24Z, so the per-class channel on the box is printing raw keys now. It does not steer any verdict — A4 diagnostics are computed and never consulted below — so this is an operator-facing defect, not a reading defect.

arbiter.word: I, the arbiter, grant T14: Eng's per-class diagnostic label names each (moduleId, eventType) class unambiguously, so that two distinct classes can never print the same label, because a diagnostic that merges two classes misreports the count it exists to explain.

conditions: PRE-REGISTRATION. The label becomes `JSON.stringify([bucket[0].moduleId, bucket[0].eventType])`. The bucket is non-empty by construction (it exists because a record fell into it), and the two components are the record's own — not re-derived, not parsed back out of the key.

⛔ THE OPENS ARE TWO FILES AND IT IS MEASURED, under the rule accepted 2026-10-01 15:15Z. Population: 43 suites, every *.test.ts under src/mica/**, src/glue/** and src/core-door/**, run with the FIX applied and compared against the relayed state dcee656: **43 OF 43 IDENTICAL — NOTHING MOVED AT ALL.** ⚠ THAT IS THE FINDING AND NOT THE REASSURANCE: no test in this repository asserts this label, so the defect was invisible to every suite and the fix is invisible too. A channel nobody asserts is a channel that can say anything. eng.test.ts is therefore opened to ADD the assertion, not because the fix moves it.

THE TEST, already written and already proven to fail without the fix: ① [T14/F1] every per-class bucket prints a DISTINCT label, on Codex's own pair — ("a", "b\u0000c") beside ("a", "b/c") — plus a third ordinary class; ② [T14/F1] the label carries the RECORD's two components, asserted as a ROUND TRIP rather than against a literal spelling, so the test survives a future change of label format without being rewritten. Mutating the label back to `key.replace` fails BOTH: 73 → 71/2.

⛔ WHAT A FAIL LOOKS LIKE: (a) two distinct classes still print one name; (b) the label is parsed back OUT of the key instead of read off the record — that is the same coupling with an extra step; (c) a fourth suite moves (43 of 43 were identical, so any movement is this change doing more than it says); (d) the struck `key.replace` line is DELETED rather than struck, as with T13's NUL comment; (e) the door reports drift on any file not in `opens`.

⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, stated so the receipt does not let SPENT imply otherwise. Codex's F2 stands: nothing in the suite enforces that Eng USES the shared tuple key rather than a private re-implementation that happens to be correct. That is the behavioural parity act already owed to the board (o6), and it is not this ticket's. Codex's F3 also stands corrected: the T13 brief said FIVE call sites and there are FOUR — I counted the definition as a call.

DIGEST-PROVEN RELAY: fix, test and repin in ONE commit (npx ts-node src/core-door/core-door.ts --propose-repin T14-eng-class-label), linear on dcee656, never an amendment of it. `--propose-repin` prints and does not write; the merge is the seat's hand and every new entry must carry THIS ticket's sha, asserted and not assumed.
